subject: Hosted API: data-dwelling, retention & deletion roadmap (Q&A)
messages:
From: Rachel Liu <r.liu@asterion.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asterion Security Team <security@asterion.ai>
Date: 2028-12-20T16:14:00Z
Subject: Hosted API: clarifications on data dwelling / erase timelines

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. As we prepare our internal security review for the Redwood hosted API, can you confirm a few specifics so we can close the section on data residency and erasure? High-level asks below — bullets are intentional:

- For customer-provided content (prompts, completions, attachments) ingested via the hosted API, where does the data physically reside by default (region/availability zones)? We need to know whether we can constrain to eu-west-1 for EU-only tenants.
- What is your retention policy for: (a) live request data (request/response), (b) inference/worker caches (KV/prefix cache), (c) logs/traces, and (d) backup snapshots? Please give SLOs for deletion after a tenant erasure request.
- Do you perform logical deletion only (metadata flag) or do you also run physical overwrite/purge from backups? If backups require a retention window, what is the maximum time data might remain in backups after a delete request?
- How are erasure requests surfaced to customers (API, console, support ticket)? Is there an audit trail we can reference to demonstrate deletion?

We appreciate any matrices / evidence you can share. If you have a short spreadsheet or diagram that maps "data type -> where stored -> deletion SLO -> evidence" that would be ideal.

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Liu
Head of Security, Asterion Health

--
Note: we need this for our compliance gate next week (deadline 2028-12-27).

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Liu <r.liu@asterion.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-12-20T19:38:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API: clarifications on data dwelling / erase timelines

Hi Rachel — thanks for the clear list. Summary first, details below; attaching a one-page matrix (redwood-data-dwelling-matrix.pdf).

TL;DR:
- Residency: For hosted customers we currently support regional residency in us-west-2, eu-west-1, and eu-central-1. You can request EU-only tenancy and we will route and store customer content exclusively in the chosen region for both primary storage and replicas.
- Retention & deletion: Live request data and model KV caches are kept for performance reasons for up to 24 hours by default (configurable to 0 hours for strict customers). Logs (token/usage traces) retained 90 days by default (can be shortened to 30). Backups/snapshots have a rolling retention of 30 days; physical deletion from backups can therefore take up to 30 days after logical removal.
- Erasure process: Customer-initiated erasures can be performed via API (/v1/tenant/erase) or through the console with documented audit trail; we also accept support-initiated erasure tickets for customers without API access. Logical deletion occurs within 24 hours; the full purge from backup snapshots completes within 30 days. We provide an erasure certificate (signed JSON blob) and a job id that you can use to verify the audit entry.

Details / mapping (short):
- Request/response payloads: stored in tenant-scoped object store in-region. Default TTL: 24h. On erasure request we remove tenant object pointers and mark blobs for purge; purge job runs nightly. Evidence: erasure certificate + audit log entry.
- KV / prefix cache: held in in-region ephemeral caches (RAM + local SSD) to accelerate repeated calls; caches are not durable and evicted within 24h. For strict compliance customers we offer cache-disabled mode (tradeoff: latency).
- Logs & traces: token-level logs used for billing and debugging live retention 90 days; can be configured to 30/60/90. If you require no logs we can offer log-minimal mode (metadata-only) and provide custom retention.
- Backups & snapshots: weekly snapshots kept for disaster recovery, rolling 30-day window for hosted. We can compress evidence of deletion via snapshot manifest. Physical bytes may persist in cold storage until snapshot rotation.
- Cross-region replication: optional and disabled by default for EU-only tenancy.

SLOs we typically quote: logical removal within 24 hours of request; manifest-level confirmation within 48 hours; physical purge from backup rotation within 30 days. If you require a contract SLA for faster irrevocable purge we can discuss a reserved-capacity/private deployment (or an expanded hosted agreement) to contractually guarantee shorter backup retention.

Next steps: please review the attached matrix — Hannah, can you add the snapshot manifest example and the erasure certificate template to the Drive link and confirm the audit log fields? Neha, can you confirm whether our EU tenancy onboarding checklist is required in the doc?

Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-data-dwelling-matrix.pdf

From: Rachel Liu <r.liu@asterion.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asterion Security Team <security@asterion.ai>
Date: 2028-12-21T08:09:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API: clarifications on data dwelling / erase timelines

Thanks — this is helpful. Two quick clarifications from the security team:

1) You mentioned KV/prefix cache is ephemeral and configurable to 0h — can you confirm whether disabling caching also removes transient copies from SSD (i.e., no writes to disk)? We need to avoid any on-disk artifacts for a subset of workloads.
2) For the erasure certificate: will that include a snapshot manifest id and the backup rotation date so we can correlate that with our internal evidence?

If you can confirm both we should be able to close the residency/retention section.

—Rachel

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Liu <r.liu@asterion.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-12-22T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API: clarifications on data dwelling / erase timelines

Hi Rachel — quick answers below and I included links to the Drive folder and the erasure cert template.

1) Cache disk artifacts: When a customer enables "cache-disabled" mode we ensure KV/prefix caching runs in-memory only. We have an implementation flag that prevents spill-to-disk; our engineering team validated the no-on-disk path for cache-disabled tenants. For highest assurance we can provide an ops runbook excerpt showing the kernel mount options and eviction behavior we apply for cache-disabled groups.

2) Erasure certificate contents: yes — the certificate contains tenant id, request timestamp, erasure job id, list of object prefixes removed, the snapshot-manifest id (if any snapshot contained the objects), and the expected snapshot-rotation date by which the bytes will be purged. We include a SHA256 of the manifest for cross-checking. Example certificate template is in Drive.

Links and artifacts: 
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cREDWOOD-data-dwelling
- Erasure cert template / example: https://drive.google.com/file/d/erasure-cert-example
- DocuSign (red-lined retention addendum): https://www.docusign.com/pack/HP-8921-retention-agreement

If that covers it I can drop a short paragraph into the compliance attestation for your SOC review. Hannah / Neha: please confirm we can share the snapshot manifest example and the ops runbook excerpt to the Drive folder (restricted link).

Thanks,
Monica
